headline: Google Home automations get surprisingly powerful with new presence sensing
summary: Google Home app now uses your phone's location and Wi-Fi to detect if you're home, enabling more advanced smart home routines.
details: Google has significantly improved its Home app's automation capabilities, making it a viable option for smart home enthusiasts without needing complex alternatives like Home Assistant.

A key new feature is expanded presence sensing, which now uses your phone's location and connected Wi-Fi networks to determine if you're home or away. Previously, this required specific Nest hardware.

This presence sensing allows for triggers like running a robot vacuum only when you're not home. You can set up automations to activate based on your location status, with options to add time conditions to avoid unwanted triggers.

The Google Clock app also integrates with Google Home, allowing routines to run automatically when you dismiss your alarm. This can include announcing weather, calendar events, turning on lights, and playing news.

Additionally, Google Home can now use the playback state of a Google TV device as an automation trigger. This allows for actions like turning off room lights when a movie starts or turning them back on when paused.
caption:

headline: College student breaks drone speed record with 491 mph jet-powered aircraft
summary: Tomas Salvo's 'Reaper' drone project, built in his dorm room, unofficially hit 491 mph, surpassing the previous record of 465 mph.
details: A college student has unofficially broken the world record for the fastest jet-powered drone. Tomas Salvo, an aerospace engineering student at Georgia Tech, built his 'Reaper' drone in his dorm room, reaching an unofficial speed of 491 mph.

The Reaper drone features a custom-molded carbon fiber shell, laser-cut internal structure, and a 250N jet engine with a 3D-printed titanium nozzle. The project cost $13,000 to build and carried a 1.2 kg payload during its record-breaking run.

Salvo's drone can maintain its top speed for four minutes on a full tank, climb to 6,500 feet in under 20 seconds, and travel 31 miles at full speed. He aims to win the $800,000 Boom Prize, which requires participants to exceed Mach 1 without on-board oxidizers or rockets.

While Salvo's speed is impressive, it has not been officially recorded by Guinness World Records. Other projects, like Mach Initiative's Kingchaser, are also competing for records and prizes, though they face eligibility challenges for the Boom Prize.

Future testing and optimizations are expected to push the Reaper's top speed past 500 mph. Salvo's project highlights the growing innovation in high-speed drone technology, driven by student projects and ambitious competitions.
